name: ULP Forth application space (bytes) — all features and device-verified

description: Baseline: shipping image after P53+P54. Metric harness validated (reproduces the baked free count exactly).

asi.harness: twin build 0.9s, checks 5.2s; app_bytes = free at MEMSZ 1688 because pool is already at 7853/7856 (headroom 0)
asi.next_action_hint: start with small mechanical text wins (pack the P54 op table 4B->2B, find() lhu fusion, wr24) to validate the loop, then the structural E1 (fold 170B code fields into header bits)

description: Specialise vm_next_ready for NTSK==2: unroll the two-slot round robin, dropping the loop and the modulo from the every-wake path. +8 B app space, text -8. Device-verified.

asi.device: flashed at MEMSZ 1696; 2 3 + . = 5, 10 FIB . = 55, 15 FIB . = ERR_STACK, 0 BLOCK . = 1568 (= BLKADR), two tasks ran, 2 3 + . = 5 after
asi.hypothesis: specialising vm_next_ready for the compile-time NTSK==2 removes a loop plus a modulo from the every-wake scheduler path
asi.measured_dead_ends: three hypotheses killed by measurement before this change: (1) hoisting V->DS is worthless because V is &vm_live, a static struct, so ds is a link-time constant; (2) the shared VM struct does NOT cost aliasing - zero reloads of the SP field inside vm_enter; (3) the P54 op table cannot be packed to 2 B (entries are function pointers) and find() cannot use an aligned lhu (the 3-byte header stride alternates parity)
asi.next_action_hint: small wins grind +8..20 B; the real prize is vm_enter (2306 B) and the only route with measured support is the asm dispatcher. Try vm_task_leave/vm_task_init specialisation next, then commit to asm

description: Literal width 6 B -> 4 B, two shapes, both regressions: (a) new LIT2 primitive = 732 B (-3: code -50 but text +38, rodata +4, plus a 3 B header for the new word); (b) halfword LIT with 0xffff escape = 731 B (-4: +48 B of dispatcher text for one inline branch). Dispatcher text is superlinear in added case logic.

asi.hypothesis: cut the cost of a literal from 6 B to 4 B, in two shapes: (a) a new LIT2 primitive carrying a halfword, (b) the existing LIT carrying a halfword with a 0xffff escape to a full cell
asi.lesson_registers: the dispatcher's text cost is SUPERLINEAR in added case logic: a 3-line branch in one case moved register allocation across the whole 2306 B switch and cost +48 B. Any change inside vm_enter must be budgeted at tens of bytes, not the few it looks like
asi.measured: (a) app 732 (-3): code -50 B, but text +38, rodata +4, and the new word cost a 3 B header - the header plus case body exceeded the saving. (b) app 731 (-4): no new word, but the inline escape in the hottest case cost +48 B of text on its own
asi.next_action_hint: do not retry literal-width work: the arithmetic is known now (ceiling ~50 B of code against 40+ B of unavoidable dispatcher text). The only lever that beats that ratio is bulk replacement of the dispatch loop itself (asm), where the per-body saving is 15 B vs 30 B across all 64 bodies instead of 2 B across 25 literals

description: blk_xfer reads the mailbox status once (it read it up to 4x after the poll, and the main core can rewrite that word between reads); mkhdr merges its two identical MSG_ERR_DICT exits. +6 B app space, text -6, dictionary unchanged, device-verified with a full block round trip.

asi.device: flashed at MEMSZ 1702: 0 BLOCK . = 1574 (= BLKADR), block write/UPDATE/SAVE round trip 65 -> reads 65, second block 66, separation intact, two tasks printed 30 and 70, 2 3 + . = 5 after
asi.harness_fix: side fix this iteration: .auto/measure.sh hardcoded MEMSZ_NOW=1688, so after keep #2 moved MEMSZ to 1696 the metric measured at the OLD value and reported 727 for a tree that had 735. It now derives MEMSZ from the built artifact (data - 16), not from a constant and not by parsing the macro
asi.hypothesis: two text cuts outside the dispatcher: (a) blk_xfer reads the mailbox status ONCE instead of up to four times, (b) mkhdr merges its two identical MSG_ERR_DICT exits into one condition
asi.measured: app 735 -> 741 (+6), text 4918 -> 4912, dictionary unchanged (code 578 + headers 255), suite 12/12, bench identical
asi.next_action_hint: text is linear outside vm_enter and superlinear inside it: prefer many small edits in main/word/find/blk_xfer over any single line in the switch. The asm dispatcher remains the only bulk lever

description: Inline the PAD-relative accesses to skip rd8/wr8's bounds check on the tokeniser path: 741 -> 637 B. The shared call wins because the call site pays the same address materialisation and the callee's arithmetic/test is shared across ~100 sites. Third local edit in a row to regress.

asi.hypothesis: bypass rd8()/wr8() for the 9 PAD-relative accesses, whose bound is provable (PAD 24 + 1 + i <= 55 < DICT 56), so the tokeniser stops paying a bounds-checked call per character
asi.lesson_inline: a shared callee beats inline code even when the inline code skips a check: the call site costs lui+addi+jal either way, and the callee's address arithmetic and bound test are shared across ~100 call sites. Inlining 9 sites cost +104 B. This is the third local edit in a row to regress (literal width, gp/small-data, PAD inlining), which is the signal that this file is at a local optimum and only structural change helps
asi.measured_other: also measured this iteration: -msmall-data-limit=2048 moves .srodata.p54_binops (56 B) into its own section but emits ZERO gp-relative references on this target, so the pool sum is unchanged (+2 B). Dead end
asi.next_action_hint: stop editing C locally. Options with arithmetic: (1) asm dispatcher - the only bulk lever, 15 B/body vs 30 B across 64 bodies; (2) two-byte dispatch table (rodata -132 B) but it requires converting 63 sweep cases from break to goto, blocked by the 5 bodies using continue/return; (3) redraw the token encoding so a token IS the primitive id, removing the 2-byte code-field read and the 128 B of primitive code fields

description: Hoist w/ip out of the VM struct into dispatch-loop locals, flushing only at the three real leaves (EXIT switch, loop-tail switch, stack-overflow return). +16 B app space, text -16, and two fewer memory round-trips per token. Device-verified including recursion, a backward loop and two task switches.

asi.device: flashed at MEMSZ 1718: 2 3 + . = 5, 10 FIB . = 55, CNT (100-iteration BEGIN..UNTIL) = 100, two tasks printed 30 and 70 (the task-switch flush path), 15 FIB . = ERR_STACK, 0 BLOCK . = 1590 (= new BLKADR), 100 7 /MOD = 14 2, 2 3 + . = 5 after
asi.hypothesis: w and ip are u16 FIELDS of the VM struct, so every token read and wrote them in memory (twice per dispatch plus once per body touching ip: LIT, BRANCH, ZBRANCH, DOCOL, EXIT, EXEC). Hoist them into locals for the dispatch loop, flush only at the three real leaves (task switch from EXIT, task switch from the loop tail, stack-overflow return)
asi.measured: app 741 -> 757 (+16), text 4912 -> 4896. Also removes 2 memory round-trips per token, so it is a speed win as well
asi.next_action_hint: same shape applies to other VM scalars that are read per token: sp and rsp are u8 FEEDLS read on every PUSH/POP/DUP. They were NOT hoisted because bodies change them constantly and the flush surface would be every return; but a smarter split (keep sp in a local, write back only at calls that can observe it) may pay. Measure before believing
asi.risk_lesson: the flush surface is the whole risk: every exit path must VM_FLUSH or the next vm_enter resumes at the previous token and silently re-executes it. Found and fixed a real sloppiness on the way: redefining the w/ip macros produced two compiler warnings on every build, now #undef'd first and the file-scope originals restored after the function

description: Fold the name hash into the copy that fills PAD (word() + the boot X-macro), deleting hash_pad entirely. Correct — 12/12 suite, bench identical — and one walk faster, but 757 -> 717 B: the 44 B function is cheaper than the two inline djb2 chains it takes to remove it.

asi.hypothesis: fold the second pass over the name into the first: word() copies and uppercases into PAD, then find() called hash_pad() to walk PAD again. Maintain the hash while copying and delete hash_pad
asi.measured: app 757 -> 717 (-40): text +36, bss +4. Deleting the 44 B hash_pad cost more than 44 B because the hash chain has to exist in TWO places (typed path in word(), boot path in the X-macro) and each inline djb2 multiply loop is ~40 B
asi.next_action_hint: the idea is functionally correct and faster (one fewer walk per token) but it loses bytes, so it loses the objective. Only revisit if the objective changes to speed. For bytes, the remaining structural options are unchanged: 2-byte dispatch table (-132 rodata, needs 63 break->goto conversions and the 5 continue/return bodies rewritten) or the asm dispatcher
asi.verdict_nuance: checks PASSED - 12/12 suite and bench identical - so this was a correct optimisation that fails only on size. Recorded as a discard for the space objective, not as a bug

description: Gate the dead depth instrumentation: vm_depth counts vm_enter entries (never exceeds 1 — DOCOL/EXEC continue the same loop) and nothing live reads it or vm_max_depth, yet both cost a compare+store per word call and two stores per exit. Kept behind -DVM_DEPTH_STATS so P13's evidence stays reproducible. +56 B app space, text -48, bss -8. Device-verified.

asi.device: flashed at MEMSZ 1774: 2 3 + . = 5, 10 FIB . = 55, CNT (100-iteration loop) = 100, 12 SQ . = 144, two tasks printed 30 and 70, 15 FIB . = ERR_STACK, 0 BLOCK . = 1646 (= BLKADR), 2 3 + . = 5 after
asi.feasibility_finding: the 2-byte dispatch table IS possible after all: a static const u16 table initialised with LABEL DIFFERENCES ('&&A - &&A') compiles on riscv32-esp-elf-gcc and emits .srodata 4 B for 2 entries with a lhu + add + jalr dispatch. Earlier I had assumed the offsets would need a runtime init (~950 B of 68 stores); that assumption was wrong and measured wrong in 30 seconds
asi.hypothesis: vm_depth and vm_max_depth are dead instrumentation: vm_depth counts ENTRIES to vm_enter (DOCOL/EXEC continue the same loop instead of recursing, so it never exceeds 1), the real nesting limit is SD 16 enforced by PUSH/RPUSH, and nothing live reads either counter. They cost a load, an add, a compare and a conditional store on every word call plus a store per exit
asi.measured: app 757 -> 813 (+56), text 4896 -> 4848 (-48), bss 877 -> 869 (-8). Biggest single win of the session
asi.next_action_hint: the 2-byte dispatch table is now proven feasible and is worth -132..134 B of rodata: 68 nested case labels become L_<NAME>, break becomes goto tail, and the 5 continue bodies become goto top. That is the next iteration

description: Replace the switch's 4-byte-address jump table with a 2-byte label-offset table (per-build width: u16 on the ULP, pointer on the host where code exceeds 64 KB). 813 -> 925 B app space; rodata 346 -> 206, text +28. Four distinct bugs found and closed on the way. Device-verified across arithmetic, recursion, loops, tasks, blocks and the error path.

asi.bugs_found: four, each caught by a loud symptom rather than silently: (1) harvesting only the first label per line left BTICK without an entry -> bake reported '[']?' because find() succeeded and the DISPATCH fell to L_BAD; (2) the table needs the SAME #if guards as the cases, and p54_subset.inc really does define P31_SUBSET, so an unguarded table failed to compile in the plain suite build; (3) an id can appear twice (p31 body gated off + P54 arm) under mutually exclusive guards, so entries must be per-occurrence; (4) the HOST build segfaulted because x86-64 code is far larger than 64 KB and a u16 offset truncated - the table width is now build-selected (u16 on ULP, pointer on HOST)
asi.device: flashed at MEMSZ 1886: 2 3 + . = 5, 7 8 * . = 56, 100 7 /MOD = 14 2, 1 2 OR = 3, 10 FIB . = 55, CNT (100-iteration loop) = 100, 12 SQ . = 144, two tasks printed 30 and 70, 15 FIB . = ERR_STACK (error path), 0 BLOCK . = 1758 (= BLKADR), 2 3 + . = 5 after
asi.hypothesis: replace GCC's 4-byte-absolute-address switch table (268 B) with a 2-byte label-offset table, now that label differences in a static initializer are proven to compile on this target
asi.measured: app 813 -> 925 (+112), rodata 346 -> 206 (-140), text 4848 -> 4876 (+28 for the bound check and the jump sequence). Table: 81 guarded entries
asi.next_action_hint: rodata is now 206 B of which the P54 op table is 56 - the dispatch table is gone. Remaining text is 4876 with vm_enter still dominant; the asm dispatcher is the only bulk lever left. Also: the dispatch now has a bounds check that the switch did not, so a corrupt token is named instead of undefined

description: Delete three write-only switch counters (read by nothing) and the vm_trace hook (never assigned, so its call site was a load + branch + indirect call that always failed). Same shape as the depth-counter win. +48 B app space, text -36, bss -12. Device-verified.

asi.device: flashed at MEMSZ 1934: 2 3 + . = 5, 10 FIB . = 55, 15 FIB . = ERR_STACK, CNT (100-iteration loop) = 100, two tasks printed 30 and 70, 0 BLOCK . = 1806 (= BLKADR), 2 3 + . = 5 after
asi.hypothesis: same shape as P56 (+56 for the depth counters): find remaining write-only instrumentation. Three switch counters (vm_switches, vm_sw_taskexit, vm_sw_first) are incremented and read by nothing, and vm_trace is a hook that nothing ever ASSIGNS, so the call site is a load + branch + indirect call that always fails
asi.next_action_hint: two levers left with arithmetic: (1) .rodata 206 B, of which the primitive NAME STRINGS are ~150 B (needed at boot to build headers, so they cannot just go - a packed blob with length bytes could halve them, and the P54 op table is 56 B); (2) the asm dispatcher, still the only bulk text lever. Also worth auditing: the remaining .bss is tsk 280 + vm_live 136 + tib 128 + rings 192 = 736 of 857
asi.search_method: the audit that found these is 3 lines: for each u32 candidate, count lines that READ it versus lines that WRITE it; a counter with reads=0 is pure cost. Worth running over every static in the file rather than one at a time

description: Third write-only audit: remove repl_line_count and repl_err_count (incremented per line/error, read by nothing anywhere in the tree) and the provably-dead x >= 2048 bound in mkhdr (the line above proves x < h <= MEMSZ, and the static assert pins the ceiling). +56 B app space, text -48, bss -8. Device-verified.

asi.ceiling_warning: IMPORTANT for the roadmap: memsz_max is now 1990 and the xt field is 10 bits of xt/2, so the code area cannot exceed 2046. _Static_assert(MEMSZ <= 2048) enforces it. Only about 58 B of further pool savings can still be banked into app space before that encoding limit binds; after that the header must move to hash12|xt11|imm1 (hash12 was measured collision-free too) to raise the ceiling to ~4096
asi.dead_end: spent part of this iteration on a WRONG assumption: I believed the 71 boot-time primitive name strings were ~150 B of .rodata and that factoring their copy loop would shrink .text. Measured: both were 0 delta because boot_init() is HOST-ONLY - the ULP build uses -DIMAGE and --gc-sections deletes it entirely, so none of the boot code is in the shipped image. Second time an unverified rodata/boot assumption cost an iteration
asi.device: flashed at MEMSZ 1990: 2 3 + . = 5, 10 FIB . = 55, 15 FIB . = ERR_STACK, CNT (100-iteration loop) = 100, two tasks printed 30 and 70, 0 BLOCK . = 1862 (= BLKADR), 100 7 /MOD = 14 2, 2 3 + . = 5 after
asi.hypothesis: run the write-only audit over the REPL harness instead of the engine: repl_line_count and repl_err_count are incremented per line/error, reset at boot, and read by NOTHING (not the HP, not the suite, not any tool); also drop the `x >= 2048u` bound in mkhdr which is provably dead given the line above proves x < h <= MEMSZ and the static assert pins MEMSZ <= 2048

description: Fourth dead-state removal: drop blkvars[BLK_VBLKERR] (written on every refused block and every xfer, read by nobody — the status reaches Forth as a pushed value and the host as a message code) and TSK.entry (written once, never read; vm.W already holds the start address). +16 B app space, text -12, bss -4. Device-verified including a full block round trip.

asi.ceiling_now_binding: memsz_max is 2006 and the xt field is 10 bits of xt/2, so the code area stops at 2046: only about 40 B of further pool savings can still be banked as app space before _Static_assert(MEMSZ <= 2048) fires. The NEXT structural change must widen xt to 11 bits (hash12|xt11|imm1; the hdr probe measured hash12 collision-free too) or further text savings buy nothing
asi.device: flashed at MEMSZ 2006: 2 3 + . = 5, 0 BLOCK . = 1878 (= BLKADR), full block round trip: write 77 + UPDATE + SAVE = 0 then 0 BLOCK C@ . = 77, 10 FIB . = 55, 15 FIB . = ERR_STACK, CNT = 100, two tasks printed 30 and 70, 2 3 + . = 5 after
asi.failed_this_iteration: moving main's boot-once block into a noinline boot_once() cost 14 B (call + worse allocation in both halves) - main is best as one function
asi.hypothesis: systematic write-only audit of every static and struct field in both source files (the audit has paid three times): found blkvars[BLK_VBLKERR] written on a refused block and on every xfer, read by nobody, and tsk[].entry written once and read by nobody
asi.measured: app 1029 -> 1045 (+16), text 4792 -> 4780 (-12), bss 849 -> 845 (-4). TSK.entry removal is text-only because struct padding absorbed the field

description: Widen the dictionary header to hash12|xt11|imm1 (still 3 bytes) so MEMSZ can pass 2046, and pay for it by deleting repl_cyc_start (an rdcycle + store on every wake into a value nothing reads). Net +4 B; ceiling lifted from 2046 to 4094. Bake's pairwise collision check passed at 12 bits; device-verified including two tasks printing 30 and 70.

asi.correction: my previous ASI claimed the xt ceiling was binding at MEMSZ 2006. It was not: the POOL was binding (it caps MEMSZ at ~2013 with this text size), and the encoding cap was 2046, i.e. ~33 B away. The lift is therefore a forward-looking enabler, not an immediate unblock - recorded so it is not oversold
asi.device: flashed at MEMSZ 2010, pool 7855/7856: 2 3 + . = 5, 0 BLOCK . = 1882 (=BLKADR), 10 FIB . = 55, 15 FIB . = ERR_STACK, CNT = 100, SPAWN TA SPAWN TB printed 3070 (both tasks ran), 100 7 /MOD = 14 2, 2 3 + . = 5 after
asi.hypothesis: widen the header to hash12|xt11|imm1 (still 3 bytes) so MEMSZ can exceed 2046, and pay for it by removing repl_cyc_start: an rdcycle plus a store executed on EVERY wake into a value nothing reads. The bake re-checks the stored keys pairwise, so a 12-bit collision aborts it instead of shipping
asi.measured: app 1045 -> 1049 (+4): the lift cost +10 B of text, the cyc_start removal returned 10 B of text and 4 B of bss
asi.near_miss: V_XEXIT and V_XSTR looked dead when I grepped uforth.c alone - they are read by the EXIT and PDOTQ case bodies in p31_cases.inc. Grepping one file nearly deleted live code; the compile caught it only because the .inc is a separate file
asi.next_action_hint: with the ceiling at 4094, the pool is now the only binding constraint, so the asm dispatcher's ~400 B is fully bankable. Two board-test lessons to keep: '.' on an empty stack wraps sp to 255 and the engine only self-heals on the next PUSH, and the task guard then refuses every spawn until reset - twice I read that as a regression when it was my test
